sections.label: Sections 11C and 11D(1) penalties
sections.summary: Sections 11C and 11D(1) carry a mandatory minimum two years' imprisonment for subsequent convictions and a maximum of 10 years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Sections 11C and 11D(1) will have a mandatory minimum imprisonment sentence of two years for subsequent convictions and a maximum imprisonment of 10 years.

sections.label: Section 11D(2) first-time penalties
sections.summary: Section 11D(2) imposes a maximum five years' imprisonment, a fine up to $10,000, or both, for first-time convictions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Section 11D(2) will impose a maximum imprisonment of five years or a fine of up to $10,000 or both, for first-time convictions.

sections.label: New offences and parental counselling
sections.summary: New offences carry up to 10 years for first-time convictions and a mandatory minimum two years for subsequent convictions, and parents or guardians of young drug abusers under CNB supervision orders must attend drug counselling.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: The new offences would carry imprisonment of up to 10 years for first-time convictions, and a mandatory minimum imprisonment of two years for subsequent convictions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Moving on to a different point, we will also mandate that parents and guardians of young drug abusers where the young drug abusers are under the Central Narcotics Bureau's (CNB’s) supervision order, the parents/guardians must attend drug counselling.

sections.label: Hair analysis in MDA
sections.summary: In 2012, hair analysis was introduced in the MDA as an alternative drug detection tool.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: In 2012, we introduced hair analysis in the MDA as an alternative drug detection tool.

sections.label: Clause 18 Director CNB power
sections.summary: Clause 18 gives the Director of CNB power to subject an abuser to rehabilitation and supervision based on a positive hair analysis result.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Clause 18 gives the Director of CNB the power to subject an abuser to rehabilitation and supervision based on the positive result of an hair analysis.

sections.label: Penalty for failure to provide
sections.summary: The punishment for failure to provide can be a maximum of two years' imprisonment, a $5,000 fine, or both.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: The punishment can be a maximum of two years' imprisonment, a $5,000 fine, or both, if there is a failure to provide.

sections.label: Drug abusers arrested yearly
sections.summary: Drug abusers arrested each year fell from just under 6,000 in 1996 to slightly over 3,000 in 2017.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: The number of drug abusers arrested each year: in 1996, roughly, just under 6,000 to now, slightly over 3,000 in 2017.

sections.label: Recidivism rates for cohorts
sections.summary: The 2015 cohort recidivism rate is 27%, down from 35% for the 2008 release cohort, but the five-year rate for LT inmates remains over 60%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: The recidivism rate for the 2015 cohort is 27%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: That is down from 35% for the 2008 release cohort.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: But, unfortunately, the five-year recidivism rate for LT inmates remains high at over 60%.

sections.label: LT-liable abusers rehabilitation channelling
sections.summary: Around 50% of LT-liable abusers could now be channelled to the rehabilitation regime.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Around 50% of LT-liable abusers could now be channelled to the rehabilitation regime.

sections.label: Clause 18 detention for rehabilitation
sections.summary: Clause 18 increases the maximum period of detention for rehabilitation from three years now to four years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Clause 18 of the Bill increases the maximum period of detention for rehabilitation; to be increased from three years now to four years.

sections.label: Clause 18 supervision duration
sections.summary: Clause 18 will increase the maximum supervision duration to five years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Clause 18 will increase the maximum supervision duration to five years.

sections.label: Clause 16 drug consumption sentence
sections.summary: Clause 16 provides a mandatory minimum sentence of one year for first-time conviction for drug consumption.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Clause 16 provides mandatory minimum sentence of one year for first-time conviction for drug consumption.

sections.label: Enhanced punishment for abusers
sections.summary: Clauses 16 and 17 give enhanced punishment or LT to convicted abusers whose current offence is drug consumption or failure to provide specimen and who have listed antecedents.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: For abusers convicted in Court, clauses 16 and 17, they will receive enhanced punishment or LT, whenever is applicable, if the current offence of which they are convicted is one of drug consumption, or failure to provide urine or hair specimen and their antecedents include any of the following: a previous conviction for drug consumption; a previous conviction for failure to provide urine or hair specimen; a previous admission into an approved institution for rehabilitation; and a previous conviction for drug consumption under the Singapore Armed Forces (SAF) Act.

sections.label: SAF officers collect urine specimens
sections.summary: Clause 13 lets appointed SAF enforcement officers collect urine from suspected abusers subject to military law, and extends detention and rehabilitation periods to 12 months, capped at four years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Clause 13 allows appointed SAF enforcement officers to collect urine specimens from persons subject to military law, if these persons are suspected abusers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: The current practice for suspected abusers is to be committed by Director CNB to a specified place for a maximum of seven days for medical examination or observation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: It also extends the initial period to which a person may be detained or rehabilitated and the period for which this may further be extended from the previous six months, now to 12 months.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: This is really to make it more streamlined, when now the detention order of every single abuser in our institutions needs to be extended every six months.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: But the total detention will not exceed four years, as I have stated earlier.

sections.label: Young drug abusers in 2017
sections.summary: In 2017, four out of 10 total drug abusers were below 30 years old.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: In 2017, four out of 10 total drug abusers were below 30 years old.

sections.label: Youth drug perception survey
sections.summary: A survey found youths aged 16 to 21 agreeing with statements about trying drugs rose from 11% in 2013 to 16% in 2016, and over 33% of youths up to 30 misperceived cannabis.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: According to the National Council Against Drug Abuse’s Youth and Public Perception Survey, the proportion of youths aged 16 to 21 who agreed with statements, such as "I do not mind trying drugs when I am overseas" and "I would try taking drugs if it was not illegal" rose from 11% in 2013 to 16% in 2016.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Over 33% of youths up to 30 years old misperceived cannabis as less harmful or non-addictive.

sections.label: New drug offences introduced
sections.summary: The Bill introduces new sections 11C and 11D prohibiting introducing a drug trafficker to another person, instructing cannabis plant cultivation, and manufacturing or consuming drugs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: To supplement drug prevention education efforts, this Bill introduces new offences in new sections 11C and 11D to prohibit introducing a drug trafficker to another person or instructing a person to cultivate plants from which cannabis can be extracted, and manufacturing or consuming drugs.

sections.label: Longer rehabilitation and supervision
sections.summary: Minimum rehabilitation becomes 12 months instead of six, maximum rehabilitation rises from three to four years, and supervision from two to five years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Instead of six months, there will be a minimum of 12 months rehabilitation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The maximum duration has also been increased from three years to four years for rehabilitation and from two years to five years for supervision.

sections.label: Director's power to commit suspects
sections.summary: The Bill extends the Director's power to commit a suspected drug addict to a specified place for up to seven days.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Currently, under section 34, the Director may require any person whom he reasonably suspects to be a drug addict to be medically examined or observed by a Government medical officer or medical practitioner.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: This Bill extends the power to committing the person to a place specified by the Director for up to seven days.

sections.label: Random spot-checks for ex-addicts
sections.summary: Clause 13 allows random spot-checks to ensure ex-addicts stay off drugs while long-term imprisonment remains available.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Clause 13 allows "random spot-checks" to ensure that ex-addicts stay off drugs while long-term imprisonment is still on the books.

sections.label: Colorado marijuana homicides and bans
sections.summary: In 2016 eight of 22 homicides had a marijuana nexus, homelessness rose 50%, and many Colorado counties and municipalities prohibited recreational marijuana.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: In 2016, eight of 22 homicides had a "marijuana nexus." And I quote again, "In most cases, robbery of marijuana was a motive, or the victim was killed during a marijuana narcotics transaction." Homelessness had also increased by 50% since marijuana was legalised.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Out of 64 counties in Colorado, 61% have prohibited or have a moratorium on recreational marijuana and, out of the 243 municipalities that have taken action on this issue, about 69% have prohibited it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: In the Netherlands, the Hague has become the first Dutch city to outlaw smoking cannabis in and around its city centre, central railway station and major shopping areas.

sections.label: Synthetic drug manufacturing in Golden Triangle
sections.summary: Regionally, synthetic drug manufacturing has surged in the Golden Triangle, especially for methamphetamine.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Regionally, there has been a surge of synthetic drug manufacturing in the Golden Triangle, especially for methamphetamine.

sections.label: Penalties for repeat drug addicts
sections.summary: Third-time addicts face up to seven years' imprisonment and six strokes, while those caught four or more times face up to 13 years and 12 strokes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Addicts who consume drugs for the third time face up to seven years' imprisonment and six strokes of the cane, while addicts caught four times or more face up to 13 years' imprisonment and 12 strokes of the cane.

sections.label: Longer DRC and supervision periods
sections.summary: The amendments raised DRC time from three to four years and the supervisory window from two to five years for random urine tests or hair samples.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In parallel, the amendments raised the time an addict can spend in the DRC from three to four years, along with the longest supervisory window from two to five years to submit himself or herself at random to the authorities for urine tests or to provide a hair sample.

sections.label: Drug addicts facing criminal charges
sections.summary: The Member asks how many drug addicts imprisoned under LT1 and LT2 regimes face concurrent criminal charges, noting the Minister earlier said about 50%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I originally intended to ask how the percentages have changed over the years and what the figures were today and, with specific reference to the amendments, how many drug addicts imprisoned under the LT1 and LT2 regimes currently face concurrent criminal charges when they were originally sentenced to long-term detention.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: But the Minister earlier shared that the figure was about 50% now.

sections.label: Support for counsellors and halfway houses
sections.summary: The Member asks how much more support counsellors, halfway house employees and volunteers will receive to keep recidivism low, though the amendments foresee no increase in public expenditure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: My second clarification, while the amendments do not foresee any increase in public expenditure, how much more support will be given to counsellors and the halfway house employees and volunteers, to help keep recidivism numbers low?

sections.label: Clause 3 contamination offences
sections.summary: Clause 3 criminalises contamination acts, including introducing a drug trafficker, teaching how to cultivate or traffic drugs, and leaving drugs within a child's easy access.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Clause 3 of the Bill introduces a number of new laws that are far-reaching and reflective of the state's uncompromising and continued hard stance against drugs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Amongst other things, it criminalises the act of contamination which facilitates or promotes drug use, including actively introducing a drug trafficker to another person, knowing that the trafficker is likely to supply him with drugs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: A person should also be guilty of a contamination offence if he teaches, instructs or provides information to another person on how to cultivate, manufacture, consume, traffic, import or export controlled drugs, such as cannabis, for example, knowing or having reason to believe that the other person intends to carry out these activities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: It makes it an offence for an adult to leave drugs or drug utensils within easy access of a child, knowing that the child is likely to be in proximate range of a drug or drug utensils.

sections.label: 2018 large drug seizures
sections.summary: In 2018 there were large drug seizures, including 8.8 kilogrammes of heroin, the largest heroin haul in three years, and a 5-kilogramme cannabis haul in June.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In 2018, a number of large drug seizures, including one 8.8 kilogrammes (kg) of heroin, the largest heroin haul in three years, and a 5-kg haul of cannabis in June that year.

sections.label: Youth views and cannabis misconceptions
sections.summary: Among youths aged 13 to 21, 16% of those polled held such views, up from about 11% in 2013, and one-third had misconceptions about cannabis.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Among youths aged 13 to 21, 16% of those polled held such views, up from about 11% in 2013.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Furthermore, one-third of the respondents had misconceptions about cannabis, believing it to have medicinal properties and overlooking its harmful side effects.

sections.label: Bill criminalises contamination acts
sections.summary: The Bill seeks to criminalise contamination acts, including teaching and instructing others about drugs and introducing a drug trafficker to a person.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The Bill seeks to criminalise acts of contamination, which include teaching and instructing others about drugs that could lead to the person carrying out drug-related crimes and usage, and introducing a drug trafficker to the person.

sections.label: Amending law on introducing drugs
sections.summary: The speaker believes the trend will grow and proposes amending the law to prohibit introducing drugs to others as a deterrent.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I believe this trend will become increasingly salient in the future.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Therefore, it is wise to amend the law to prohibit the act of introducing drugs to others.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Although such behaviours are difficult to spot, having such laws would serve as a deterrent.

sections.label: Equipping youth and counselling addicts
sections.summary: The speaker says young people should be given information to decide to stay away from drugs and addicts need more counselling.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The correct way is to equip the young people with sufficient information so that they can decide for themselves to stay away from drugs.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: More counselling will help the drug addicts to kick the habit.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: However, do we have enough Prison counsellors, do we have enough support for the mental health of the counsellors themselves?

sections.label: Errant prescribers censured, fined, suspended
sections.summary: The SMC Annual Report 2012-2017 shows an average of two to three errant prescribers censured, fined and suspended yearly for inappropriate prescribing or sale.

sentences.speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: According to the Singapore Medical Council (SMC) Annual Report from 2012-2017, there is an average of two to three cases of errant prescribers who were being censured, fined and suspended every year due to inappropriate prescribing or sale of hynoptics, codeine-containing preparations or controlled drugs.

sections.label: Dispensing separation for controlled drugs
sections.summary: The passage asks whether MOH or MHA will consider dispensing separation for controlled drugs and drugs of abuse to deconflict prescribing and dispensing.

sentences.speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In contrast, as prescriptions in public hospitals and polyclinics are limited by information technology (IT) system restriction and second layer of screening by pharmacists, this problem is almost non-existent." Are there plans for MOH or MHA to consider dispensing separation for controlled drugs and other drugs of abuse, including hypnotics and codeine-containing preparations, to deconflict prescribing and dispensing of such drugs with potential for abuse?

sections.label: Cannabis legalised or decriminalised abroad
sections.summary: Cannabis is legalised for recreational use in Uruguay, Canada and eight US states, and decriminalised in several other countries.

sentences.speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Cannabis is now legalised for recreational use in Uruguay, Canada and eight other states in the US, while decriminalised in the Netherlands, Spain, Portugal, Jamaica, Slovenia and Columbia within recreational limits.

sections.label: Patients prescribed medicinal cannabis entering Singapore
sections.summary: The passage asks how Singapore plans to handle patients prescribed First Schedule Class A drugs, such as medicinal cannabis, who intend to enter Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Lastly, with medicinal cannabis now legalised in 44 countries worldwide, each claiming their benefits for certain intractable medical conditions, though yet to be proven but there are increasing clinical trials, how do we plan on handling patients prescribed with First Schedule Class A drugs, for example, cannabis for medicinal purposes, if they intend to enter Singapore?

sections.label: Anti-drug firmness with rehabilitation
sections.summary: The speaker welcomes an amendment that stays firm on anti-drug efforts while hoping to strengthen rehabilitation of drug addicts.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: It will be good if we can stop this addiction and help former addicts rebuild their lives early on.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Therefore, I truly welcome this amendment which remains firm with anti-drug efforts, and yet at the same time, will hopefully further strengthen efforts to rehabilitate drug addicts.

sections.label: Calibrated approach to pure abusers
sections.summary: The Bill takes a targeted and calibrated approach towards pure abusers who commit no other concurrent offences.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: In particular, I note that in this Bill, there is a targeted and calibrated approach towards pure abusers who do not commit other concurrent offences.

sections.label: Rehabilitation to cut addict recidivism
sections.summary: The speaker says drug addiction causes many social problems and hopes stronger rehabilitation reduces recidivism rates among addicts.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Drug addiction is the root cause of many social problems and it is important that we give enough attention to rehabilitation efforts.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: I am glad that the Ministry is working towards strengthening the rehabilitation regime and I hope that this effort translates into further reductions in the recidivism rates among addicts.

sections.label: Criminalising contamination and exposing children
sections.summary: The speaker commends provisions criminalising acts of contamination and acts exposing children and permitting young children to consume drugs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: The other aspect of this Bill which I would like to commend on are the provisions relating to the criminalisation of acts of contamination and acts exposing children and permitting young children to consume drugs.

sections.label: Punishing those who expose young people
sections.summary: The speaker is pleased that efforts curb exposing and giving drugs to young people, who may lack maturity to respond to such influences.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Apparently, this is not an uncommon story in that particular area, and other participants in the group also shared about young people they know who had access to drugs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: These young people may not have the maturity or savviness to respond appropriately to the influences.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: I am, therefore, pleased that efforts are being made to curb the irresponsible conduct of exposing and giving drugs to young people, and those who commit these acts that could ruin the future of our young ones would receive the necessary punishment.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: I believe that the implementation of this Bill will preserve our strong anti-drug position and allow for a more meaningful management of misuse of drugs in Singapore.

sections.label: Sections 11B(1) and 11B(2) penalties
sections.summary: Section 11B(1) punishes adults 21 and above who expose children to prohibited drugs or paraphernalia; 11B(2) punishes adults who allow child drug use.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Section 11B (1) is meant to punish adults, that is, individuals who are 21 years old and above, who expose children to any prohibited drug or paraphernalia that is used to consume prohibited drugs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In addition, section 11B (2) is meant to punish adults who allow a child to use any prohibited drugs, and adults who did not take any steps to prevent the child from doing so.

sections.label: Flexibility in reporting time
sections.summary: The speaker hopes individuals ordered to report themselves can choose their reporting time so it does not affect their working hours.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Regarding this issue, I hope that individuals who are ordered to report themselves are given the flexibility to choose the reporting time so that it does not affect their working hours.

sections.label: Separating rehabilitation paths by risk
sections.summary: The amendment separates the rehabilitation path for first-time low and medium risk offenders from those at high risk of reoffending.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For this group, even the smallest emotional disturbance can cause excessive stress to them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This amendment separates and differentiates the rehabilitation path or process for first-time offenders with low and medium risk, from those who are at a high risk of reoffending.

sections.label: Enhanced Direct Supervision Order framework
sections.summary: Low-risk first-time abusers go on the Enhanced Direct Supervision Order with a case manager and counselling, while moderate or high risk and repeat abusers attend DRC programmes.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Under the new proposed framework, first-time abusers assessed to be of low risk will, instead, be placed on the Enhanced Direct Supervision Order (EDSO), a non-custodial supervision order, get assigned a case manager and undergo counselling.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Only first-time abusers with moderate or high risk of further abuse, as well as those arrested for the second time and above will go through programmes of varying degrees of intensity and durations at the DRC.

sections.label: 2015 Youth and Drugs survey results
sections.summary: The speaker is worried by the 2015 survey by the Task Force on Youth and Drugs, which found some academically good young people from middle and upper middle-class families abusing drugs.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I am particularly worried by the results of the 2015 survey commissioned by the Government's Task Force on Youth and Drugs.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: It found that even some of the young with good academic results from middle and upper middle-class families are abusing drugs.

sections.label: Deterrence and calibrated rehabilitation approach
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether harsher penalties like detention would deter drug use, supports the calibrated approach, and seeks assurance the amendments still signal a firm approach.

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Would harsher penalties, such as detention, be more effective deterrents so they do not get started on drugs at all?

sentences.speaker: Dr Chia Shi-Lu (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I do support this more calibrated approach in principle and welcome the increased focus on rehabilitation for drug offenders, but would seek the Minister's assurance that these amendments still signal a firm approach towards drug abuse.

sections.label: Offence of exposing children to drugs
sections.summary: The speaker says rehabilitation is the only way to restore lives affected by drug abuse, and the Bill implements a new section 11B making it an offence to expose or permit young children to consume drugs.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Rehabilitation is the only way to restore the lives of those affected by drug abuse.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This Bill implements a new section 11B which makes it an offence to expose or permit young children to consume drugs.

sections.label: Drugs hidden without lock
sections.summary: An abuser who hid drugs at home accessible to a child without lock and key would face up to 10 years.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As worded, an abuser who merely hid their drugs at home in a place accessible by a child, but without lock and key, would have committed an offence punishable with a term of up to 10 years.

sections.label: Disparate impact on poor abusers
sections.summary: Financially able drug users can afford separate living quarters and avoid section 11B(1), while impoverished abusers living with family may offend.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Their family may be torn between the risks of living with a drug abuser and their desire to support a family member.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: There is disparate impact if a financially able drug user who can afford separate living quarters, is under no risk of being charged under section 11B(1), but a financially impoverished drug abuser may offend under section 11B(1) because they must live in a family setting.

sections.label: Evidence for section 11B policy
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Minister to discuss evidence linking reckless exposure to youth drug abuse and related statistics.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Policies, such as section 11B, must be based on empirical evidence from drug abuse policing and intervention that shows a causal link between reckless exposure and subsequent drug abuse by the youth.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: So, I hope, in this regard, the Minister can discuss the evidence on the number and proportion of drug offenders in family settings where children are at risk; proportion of cases where investigating officers found that the drug offender was recklessly exposing their family to drugs and the number of youths whose drug abuse appears to be linked to such family exposure.

sections.label: Support and evidence for 11B(1)
sections.summary: The speaker suggests MSF reports before charges and asks how stronger measures rest on evidence, urging public research.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For example, it could enhance welfare if the CNB and Public Prosecutor would, before deciding whether to proceed with a charge under 11B(1), call for a report from the Ministry of Social and Family Development's (MSF's) Child Protective Service or other relevant authorities.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In addition, if we are prepared to enact stronger legal measures against the drug abuser who puts his family at risk, then we must also be prepared to provide further assistance for that family, especially if a breadwinner may be incarcerated for a longer period.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: That social support is based on the principle that we are protecting society – which includes drug abusers and their families – from the harms caused by drug abuse.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I hope the Minister can outline how the stronger measures in 11B(1) are based on the evidence that such reckless exposure to young children is prevalent, increases the risks of youth drug abuse, and it can be effectively deterred by 11B(1) for the greater welfare of the families affected.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In particular, I think both the Ministry and society would benefit from more public research by Singapore-based academics on our criminal justice system.

sections.label: CNB 2017 arrest statistics
sections.summary: CNB statistics show 3,091 drug abusers arrested in 2017, 40% new, two-thirds of new abusers under 30.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Based on statistics by CNB, 3,091 drug abusers were arrested in 2017; 40% were new drug abusers and two-thirds of the new abusers were under the age of 30.

sections.label: Same case officer for inmates
sections.summary: Minister K Shanmugam announced SPS will look into assigning inmates the same case officer from sentence start to community integration.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: On integration, Minister K Shanmugam recently announced that SPS will look into assigning inmates the same case officer from the start of their sentence until they are fully integrated into the community.

sections.label: Urine test reporting timings
sections.summary: Former drug offenders report at fixed timings in batches for urine tests, sometimes up to three times a week, affecting their livelihood.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I have learnt from ex-drug offenders that they have to report at fixed timings where they are clustered into batches to take their urine test.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This affects the livelihood of these former drug offenders as they have to take time off work to take the urine tests, sometimes up to three times a week.

sections.label: Flexible testing and community support
sections.summary: The speaker asks about flexible urine test timings, commends anti-drug community efforts and pro-rehabilitation changes in the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Even if a person wants to stay clean and away from drugs, the lure of bad company might lead them back to drugs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Therefore, is there a possibility to allow the supervisees to report for urine tests at flexible timings without being clustered into groups?

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Support from the community remains an integral part in the fight against drugs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I commend efforts, such as CNB's United Against Drugs Coalition (UADC), an anti-drug coalition made up of local organisations and business enterprises.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I would also like to highlight the good work undertaken by ReviveSG, a ground-up initiative formed in 2017 by a group of former drug-related offenders and renounced gang members.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: ReviveSG not only provides support and counselling to youths-at-risk, they also conduct recovery programmes and educational programmes for parents, educators, employers and the public.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In light of the daunting journey that a former drug offender faces after he leaves prison, I commend the pro-rehabilitation changes proposed in this Bill.

sections.label: No softening of anti-drug stance
sections.summary: The speaker welcomes MDA amendments but says Singapore's anti-drug zero-tolerance stance must not be softened.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: While I welcome the amendments to the MDA, we must ensure that, first, there must be no softening of Singapore's anti-drug zero-tolerance stance.

sections.label: Distinguishing abusers from other offenders
sections.summary: The proposed amendments distinguish between abusers who only consume drugs and those who also commit offences harming society.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: The proposed amendments are founded upon distinguishing between abusers who only consume drugs and those who concurrently commit other offences of harm to society.

sections.label: Cap on DRC repeat offenders
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether MHA would cap how many times a repeat offender without other offences can go through DRC before LT.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Under the proposed amendments, a repeat offender who does not commit other criminal offences would only go through the DRC regime without LT.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Would MHA consider setting a cap on the number of times an offender can go for the DRC regime before LT sets in?

sections.label: Adults' role in child drug rehabilitation
sections.summary: The speaker supports clauses 3 and 19, which emphasise adults' responsibility and parents' involvement in a young person's drug recovery.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The fact remains that significant adults in a child’s life have that role and responsibility to ensure our children stay away from drugs and have significant influence towards a child's propensity and attitude towards drug use.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Hence, I strongly support clauses 3 and 19 of this Bill.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Clause 3 of the Bill places greater emphasis on the responsibility needed by the adults within the family to ensure the home remains a safe and drug-free place for our children.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Clause 19 requires the involvement of parents and guardians to be included in the counselling sessions, not to punish them, but to ensure the rehabilitation process remains an integrated and positive approach involving the significant adults in a young person's drug recovery journey.

sections.label: Rehabilitation, enforcement and SAF drug testing
sections.summary: The speaker seeks assurance that rehabilitation for young abusers does not weaken enforcement, supports clause 13 on SAF urine testing, and asks about stricter action for drug use in MINDEF premises.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In addition, while I support the emphasis on rehabilitation for young drug abusers, may I seek the Ministry’s assurance that it does not mean we are going soft on drug abuse and related crimes and that enforcement action will continue to be robust and will be meted out without fear or favour?

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I am confident that with these new measures being legislated, proactive and educational approaches will also be enhanced to ensure we can keep our children safe from drugs through awareness and prevention, rather than just through the enforcement of enacted laws.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I also support clause 13 that confers powers on certain SAF servicemen to assume the role of enforcement officers and request for urine samples from suspected servicemen for urine tests to be conducted.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Through their appeal to the Ministry of Defence (MINDEF), they asked for stricter enforcement in requiring servicemen to be tested for drug use, even though the drug use was not in the camp itself.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: However, I would like to ask if there are even stricter enforcement actions to be taken if the drug use is discovered within any of our MINDEF premises or camps by SAF servicemen or regulars?

sections.label: Drugs within reach of children
sections.summary: The speaker welcomes clause 3, which makes adults responsible for drug-free homes and imposes heavier punishment for allowing children to reach drugs.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: What is more worrying is the presence of their small children in the house, whereby the father or mother is taking drugs right in front of their children and those drugs are within easy reach to these children.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Therefore, I welcome the amendments to the Act whereby clause 3 underlines the responsibility of adults in the family to ensure that our homes stay drug-free for the sake of our children.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: A heavier punishment will be given to those found guilty, for instance, for allowing drugs in the house to be easily reached by their children, especially those who are minors.

sections.label: Mandatory minimum for first-time offenders
sections.summary: New section 33(3A) prescribes a mandatory minimum one-year sentence for first-time drug possession or consumption offenders, shifting from the current no-minimum position and six-to-eight-month norm.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: First, the Bill proposes a new section 33(3A), which prescribes a mandatory minimum sentence of one year for first-time offenders of a section 8 offence of drug possession or consumption.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: This represents quite a shift from the status quo currently where there is no prescribed minimum sentence and, therefore, a Court is entitled to impose a sentence of a fine and/or a jail term of less than one year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The present sentencing norm for first-time drug consumption is between six and eight months’ imprisonment.

sections.label: Supervision duration increased to five years
sections.summary: Section 34 increases the duration of supervision from two years to five years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Section 34 deals with the increased duration of supervision from two years to five years.

sections.label: Reuniting families and supervision resourcing
sections.summary: The speaker says reuniting drug-fractured families is a good objective, notes the Explanatory Note states no increase in public expenditure, but anticipates resourcing and staffing issues from supervision of up to five years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: This would be a good objective to realise because families fractured by their members who take drugs can then have a chance to be wholly reunited again.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I note that the Explanatory Note suggests that there is no increase in public expenditure arising from the amendments to this Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: However, I would imagine that there would be resourcing and staffing issues, given that the contemplated extension of supervision is for a period of up to five years.

sections.label: US drug problem and fentanyl
sections.summary: The speaker recounts Ms Bridget Brennon's report that US life expectancy fell for three consecutive years due to the drug problem, worsened by synthetic drugs like fentanyl, which is very addictive and costs a fifth of heroin.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I had occasion to listen to the speech of Ms Bridget Brennon, the Special Prosecutor for Narcotics in the city of New York in the US last year at the Economic Crime Symposium in Cambridge, UK.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: She reported that, in the US, life expectancy has gone down for three consecutive years and she attributed it to the serious drug problem her country has.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The situation has been exacerbated by the advent of synthetic drugs, such as fentanyl, which is very addictive and only a fifth of the cost of heroin.

sections.label: Mandatory minimum sentences amendments
sections.summary: The amendments codify a rehabilitative approach, introduce mandatory minimum sentences under section 33, and expand section 33A enhanced penalties for repeat offenders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: These amendments will codify the rehabilitative approach and align our legislative framework with ground initiatives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I note that section 33 will be amended to introduce mandatory minimum sentences for offences of consuming controlled or specified drugs, failing to provide urine specimens and failing to provide hair specimens.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Further, section 33A on enhanced penalties for repeat offenders will be expanded.

sections.label: DRC visit quota usage
sections.summary: At the DRC, only a third of inmates use their full quota of two 30-minute visits per month.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: At the DRC, I understand that only a third of inmates use their full quota of two 30-minute visits per month.

sections.label: Mandatory counselling for parents
sections.summary: New section 34A will require parents and guardians to undergo mandatory counselling together with young offenders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The new section 34A will require parents and guardians to undergo mandatory counselling together with young offenders.

sections.label: Criminalising drug contamination acts
sections.summary: The passage supports criminalising acts of contamination that promote drug use and acts exposing children to drugs or allowing young persons to consume drugs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Criminalising acts of contamination which facilitate and promote use of drugs is necessary to stop the transmission of the "infection", which is the spread of drug use and addiction.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I also fully support the amendments which criminalise acts which expose children to drugs and allow young persons to consume drugs.

sections.label: Checkpoint measures and rehabilitation focus
sections.summary: The passage asks the Minister to elaborate on checkpoint measures against drug entry and notes the Bill's focus on enhancing rehabilitation and keeping abusers drug-free.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Would the Minister elaborate on measures at our checkpoints to prevent the entry of drugs into Singapore?

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Last, I noticed that a focus in this Bill is to enhance rehabilitation of drug abusers and to ensure that they stay drug-free.

sections.label: Support for new section 11B
sections.summary: The passage expresses support for new section 11B, which it says tackles intergenerational drug use, in line with statutory prohibition against drug misuse.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: They are in line with the current framework of statutory prohibition against drug misuse.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I would like to take this opportunity to express my support, in particular, for the new section 11B which, to my mind, tackles the undesirable but unfortunately rampant phenomenon of intergenerational drug use.

sections.label: Inter-Ministerial task force on drugs
sections.summary: The speaker urges the Government to commission an inter-Ministerial task force for a public education campaign and Singapore-based research on drug misuse.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Learning from this, I urge the Government to consider commissioning an inter-Ministerial task force for our "War on Drugs" to undertake the following.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: One, conduct a large-scale public education campaign to (a) educate the general public on the newly-introduced provisions, their underlying rationales and the increased severity of drug offences to ensure the deterrent intent of the amendments is well understood, and at the same time, (b) encourage destigmatisation of drug addiction to complement our calibrated rehabilitative approach.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Two, commission research, based in Singapore, which can be used to guide, strengthen and reinforce our national policies on drug misuse, ensuring they are aligned and remain up to date with neurobiological advancements and upstream prevention through public health education on substance abuse and mental health conditions.

sections.label: Questions on drug clauses
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Minister how the seven-year period was arrived at, whether section 34(1) places should be scheduled, and what counselling clause 19 envisions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Third, with regard to clause 18(a), I wish to ask the Minister how the number of seven years was arrived at for determining the period not exceeding which any person reasonably suspected to be a drug addict may be committed for the purposes of medical examination or observation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Further, I would like to ask the Minister if it would be more appropriate and prudent for the broad phrasing of the proposed section 34(1) which states "to any place specified by the Director for the purpose of any medical examination or observation" to be amended to (a) reflect a scheduled or predetermined list of places, and (b) reflect that the medical examination or observation be for the purposes of determining whether traces of drug remain in a person’s body.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Lastly, clause 19 requires a parent/guardian to attend any counselling session with a supervisee who is below 21 years of age.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I wish to ask the Minister what type of counselling this section envisions.

sections.label: CNB statistics on new abusers
sections.summary: CNB statistics state that 40% of drug abusers arrested in 2017 were new abusers, and about 64% of these were below 30.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: According to statistics by CNB, 40% of drug abusers arrested in 2017 were new abusers, and about 64% of these new abusers arrested were below 30 years of age.

sections.label: Exposing under-30s to drugs
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether the Ministry would make it an offence to expose persons below 30 to drugs and drug utensils, and suggests compulsory counselling for immediate family members.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Given that a significant number of new abusers arrested were below 30, would the Ministry consider making it an offence to expose persons below 30 to drugs and drug utensils, rather than just confining to young children?

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: On the topic of intergenerational addiction, I would like to suggest that the Ministry make it compulsory for all immediate family members to be counselled, if there is a young drug abuser in the family.

sections.label: Mandatory counselling for family members
sections.summary: The speaker suggests mandatory counselling for immediate family members below the age of 21 of adult offenders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: For adult offenders, I would also like to suggest mandatory counselling for immediate family members below the age of 21.

sections.label: CNB investigations and drug exposure
sections.summary: CNB will investigate ownership of drugs found in a household, and adults who knowingly or recklessly leave drugs exposed to children may be prosecuted.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: CNB will carry out due investigations to establish the ownership of the drugs found in the household.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Any adult who is in possession of the illicit drugs and knowingly or recklessly leaves the drug exposed, knowing that the child is likely to have access, may be prosecuted for this offence.

sections.label: Age cutoff of 16
sections.summary: Section 11B(1) is intended to protect younger children who may not understand drug dangers and risk accidental ingestion.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: To answer Mr Melvin Yong's and Ms Anthea Ong's question on the age cutoff of 16, section 11B(1) is intended to protect younger children who may not understand the dangers of drugs and are at higher risk of accidental ingestion.

sections.label: CNB counselling programme structure
sections.summary: CNB worked with social service providers to structure a counselling programme of at least 25 sessions lasting up to a year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: CNB has worked with social service providers to structure the counselling programme.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: It consists of a minimum of 25 sessions and lasts up to a year.

sections.label: Proposed section 11(D)(1) knowledge requirement
sections.summary: Proposed section 11(D)(1) requires the information provider to know or have reason to believe the recipient intends to manufacture.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: The proposed section 11(D)(1) requires that the person who provides the information knows, or has reason to believe, that the recipient intends to carry out the manufacturing.

sections.label: LT offender recidivism and supervision
sections.summary: Two-year recidivism rates for LT offenders fell from 38% to 27%, and post-release supervision for abusers will increase to a maximum of five years.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: The two-year recidivism rates for LT offenders have come down from 38% for the 2012 release cohort to 27% for the 2015 one.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Given how instrumental post-release support is in helping repeat offenders turn over a new leaf, we are doing more on this front, including increasing post-release supervision for abusers to a maximum of five years.

sections.label: Detention and supervision for poor progress
sections.summary: A person showing very poor progress may be detained up to four years in DRC for rehabilitation, with five years of supervision.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: If the person shows very poor progress, he may be detained for up to four years in DRC for rehabilitation, coupled with five years of supervision.

sections.label: Family programmes in prisons
sections.summary: SPS will restructure prison family programmes and work with MSF to identify inmates' family needs early and increase family involvement in rehabilitation.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: We recognise the importance of families to the rehabilitation process.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Hence, SPS will be restructuring family programmes in the prisons and working with MSF to identify inmates’ family needs early, provide intervention and increase family involvement in inmate rehabilitation.

sections.label: Drug offences involving children
sections.summary: New MDA amendments make it an offence for adults to leave illicit drugs within a child's access or let a young person consume drugs in their possession, and require counselling for parents of youth abusers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: The new amendments to the MDA will thus make it an offence for an adult who possesses illicit drug to knowingly or recklessly leave it within the access of a child.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: It will also be an offence for an adult who does not take reasonable steps to prevent a young person from consuming illicit drugs in the adult's possession.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: The new punitive measures will prevent these tragedies from further happening.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: We are also ensuring better support for young drug abusers and helping them turn over a new leaf by making it compulsory for parents/guardians of youth drug abusers who are under CNB's supervision order to attend counselling.

sections.label: First-time DRC inmates
sections.summary: Around 55% or 750 of the end-2017 DRC inmate population are first-timers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
sentences.text: Based on the end-2017 DRC inmate population, around 55% or 750 are first-timers.

sections.label: Mandatory minimum sentence intent
sections.summary: The primary intent of the mandatory minimum sentence is to reflect the strong deterrent stance against drugs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
sentences.text: The primary intent of the mandatory minimum sentence is to reflect the strong deterrent stance against drugs.

sections.label: Operation Lionfish seizures
sections.summary: Last year CNB joined foreign-agency operations including INTERPOL-coordinated Operation Lionfish across 93 countries, seizing over 55 tonnes of illicit drugs and arresting 1,300 suspects.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
sentences.text: Last year, CNB took part in a number of operations with foreign agencies, including Operation Lionfish, an INTERPOL-coordinated operation across 93 countries, which led to a combined seizure of more than 55 tonnes of illicit drugs and the arrest of 1,300 suspects.

sections.label: Access to computers, encrypted information
sections.summary: Authorities are empowered under the Criminal Procedure Code to access computers and encrypted information as part of investigations.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
sentences.text: Authorities are empowered under the Criminal Procedure Code to access computers and encrypted information as part of investigations.

sections.label: Pre-trip briefings for students
sections.summary: CNB works with Institutes of Higher Learning on pre-trip briefings reminding students going abroad of drug harms and that Singaporeans and Permanent Residents who consume illicit drugs overseas can be dealt with as if consumed in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
sentences.text: CNB works closely with the Institutes of Higher Learning to conduct regular pre-trip briefings for students who are going abroad.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
sentences.text: This is to remind them of the harms of drugs, and also that Singaporeans and Permanent Residents who consume illicit drugs overseas can be dealt with as if they have consumed them in Singapore.

sections.label: Traveller cannabinoid medication applications
sections.summary: Applications by travellers to bring in cannabinoid medications are considered case-by-case and must be pharmaceutical cannabinoids prescribed by qualified medical practitioners.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
sentences.text: Specific to travellers who request to bring in cannabinoid medications, these applications are considered on a case-by-case basis, and they must be pharmaceutical cannabinoids which are prescribed by qualified medical practitioners.

sections.label: CNB and HSA NPS testing
sections.summary: CNB works with agencies like HSA to expand NPS testing and shorten development time, leading to more NPS abusers and traffickers arrested in 2018.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
sentences.text: CNB is also working closely with partner agencies, such as HSA, to expand the range of NPS that can be tested and shorten the time taken to develop these testing capabilities.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
sentences.text: This has led to a significant increase in NPS abusers and traffickers arrested in 2018, and we are monitoring the situation very closely.

sections.label: SAF servicemen drug abuse charges
sections.summary: SAF servicemen caught abusing drugs are charged in the Military Court and receive custodial sentences depending on each case's facts and circumstances.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
sentences.text: In line with this zero-tolerance approach, SAF servicemen who are caught abusing drugs will be charged in the Military Court and receive custodial sentences, the duration of which would depend on the facts and circumstances of each case.

sections.label: Rehabilitation regime for drug takers
sections.summary: Those who only take drugs and admit to it can be placed under rehabilitation, undergoing intensive rehabilitation at the DRC and supervision of up to five years.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
sentences.text: We are grateful for the support from Members of Parliament on our tough stance towards drugs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
sentences.text: Those who only take drugs and admit to taking drugs, can be placed under the rehabilitation regime.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
sentences.text: They will undergo intensive rehabilitation at the DRC and a longer supervision period of up to five years.

sections.label: Protecting children from drugs
sections.summary: It will be an offence for adults to let drugs come within reach of children or let under-21s consume their drugs, and parents of drug-abusing youths must attend counselling.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
sentences.text: Third, we will double our efforts to protect our children.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
sentences.text: It will be an offence for adults who possess drugs to, either on purpose or otherwise, allow the drugs to come within reach of children.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
sentences.text: It will be an offence for adults who allow young persons under 21 to consume drugs owned by that adult.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
sentences.text: We will also require parents and guardians of youths who abuse drugs to attend counselling.

sections.label: Drug arrests decline since 1996
sections.summary: Arrests fell from nearly just under 6,000 people in 1996 to just about 3,000 now.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: As I said earlier, from nearly about just under 6,000 people being arrested in 1996, we are now down to just about 3,000.

sections.label: Rehabilitation evidence and young abusers
sections.summary: Nearly two-thirds of new abusers are under 30, and a body of evidence-based rehabilitation work led to this move.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Today, nearly two-thirds of the new abusers are under 30.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Also, over a period of time, we have built a substantive body of evidence-based work on rehabilitation based both on international experience and local research, counselling techniques, psychological interventions, evidence-based programming and technology, and the importance of family involvement, stable employment and the crucial nature of extended post-release support.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: So, today, we decided that we will make this move.

sections.label: Drug-free Singapore philosophy
sections.summary: The philosophy of a drug-free Singapore has not changed.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Fundamentally, our philosophy of a drug-free Singapore has not changed.

sections.label: Death penalty and trafficker quantities
sections.summary: The passage notes sparing thought for victims and that 15 grammes of diamorphine can feed around 180 abusers for a week.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: We could well put the drug abuser who killed her in the heart of our policies, but I think we should also spare a thought for the Noi Nois of this world.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: It is often pointed out by the Singapore Government, in the context of the death penalty, the 15 grammes of diamorphine or pure heroin that a trafficker brings in is enough to feed around 180 drug abusers for one week.

sections.label: DRC, CBP and testing
sections.summary: Admitting abusers undergo up to four years in a DRC, then CBP and longer supervision, with possible CNB urine or hair tests.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: For those who only consume drugs and admit to their drug abuse, rather than staying in LT, as we said, they will undergo a shorter but a more intensive rehabilitation in a DRC which could be up to four years and then be placed on CBPs and then a longer supervision period.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: To make sure we are able to intervene as soon as possible if they do relapse, even after they are released from supervision, the Director of CNB can require abusers who have completed their rehabilitation supervision or imprisonment to still report to CNB for urine or hair tests, when required.

sections.label: Counselling for parents of young abusers
sections.summary: Parents and guardians of young drug abusers are mandated to attend counselling.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Young people who are already on drugs, we must provide them with the support to get out of that cycle as quickly as possible.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Hence, the change to mandate parents and guardians of young drug abusers to attend counselling.
